newsitem.title: USA: Hilton holders set to approve Bally deal.
newsitem.headline: Hilton holders set to approve Bally deal.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp shareholders are expected to approve the merger with Bally Entertainment Corp Thursday, significantly expanding its gaming operations.

However, industry analysts say its new position as the largest gaming operator in the United States forces Hilton to face some hard questions about positioning its hotels and casinos to compete in an increasingly crowded marketplace.
Hilton originally announced the deal to acquire Bally Entertainment in June for more than $2 billion.
With at least six major hotels being developed, expansion of current hotels ongoing and two new major hotels opened this summer, Las Vegas will see an influx of over 23,000 new rooms through 1998.
Financial analysts, while expressing concern about excess supply, are questioning operators' ability to target their casinos toward specific customers.
"I'm not as worried about capacity expansion as I am concerned about individual properties being presented as a product," said Jeff Logsdon, analyst with Cruttenden, Roth.

Bally is developing a major new hotel/casino in Las Vegas, called "Paris", built on a theme around the French capital, and financial analysts believe Hilton may expand the property beyond its original $420 million, 2,500-room plan.
Hilton may also choose to fine tune the Paris theme to compete with new resorts being built by MGM Grand Inc, Mirage Inc.
In addition, Hilton may change the name on Bally's Las Vegas, replacing it with Hilton to re-position it as a more upscale operation on the famous Las Vegas Strip, market sources said.

Separately, oddsmakers tell investors to look for additional acquisitions from deal-maker and Hilton Chief Executive Officer Stephen Bollenbach, who was hired in February from Walt Disney Co to jazz up Hilton.
Though analysts differ on the timing and size of possible acquisitions, there is no doubt Bollenbach will target other hotel or gambling chains.
Market pros don't expect any major announcement about acquisitions at Thursday's meeting, but at least one said Bollenbach's ambition shouldn't be underestimated.
"He's always full of surprises," said Marvin Roffman of Roffman Miller Associates. "But I would hate to see any kind of major new thing. Their plate is filled."
Lastly, investors are looking for any kind of hint Hilton might expand its recently announced alliance with Ladbroke Group Plc to expand Hilton International.
On Wednesday, Bally shareholders voted to approve the merger.
